answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is pricing identity creation on scarce work history: each agent must burn verified compute or capital to earn reputation points before it can join payouts, and those points are non-transferable and tied to real completed tasks. Attacking means running thousands of fake agents, each paying real GPU and transaction costs like copper wire in a circuit, seeding a grove of identities that each must grow fruit before earning anything, so a garden of bots costs far more than any reward.
